proposed_facts.reason: Canonical callback branches confirm error-before-cancellation ordering, sector-boundary subtraction, completion before offset/FAT advancement, successor validation, and clear-release-notify cleanup. CARDRdwr.c independently confirms initialization and per-successful-segment advancement of the destination pointer.

Seek, access checks, cache invalidation, callback installation, bounded initial transfer, and continuation match canonical source. The corrected conditional advancement and potentially negative successful residual agree with functionality.md. Startup failures return directly rather than entering ReadCallback cleanup.

Canonical source distinguishes assertions from runtime guards and initial transfer failure from callback termination. Cancellation is interrupt-protected and requires attachment, BUSY state, and identical file pointer; incoming callback errors take precedence over its negative-length marker. Negative length after boundary subtraction is correctly distinguished from cancellation.

contradictions.reason: The superseded ReadCallback data-flow claim required qualification: subtraction measures the distance to the next sector boundary, and exhaustion bypasses offset/block advancement. Proposal fact 0 resolves this and correctly attributes destination advancement to the lower transfer layer.

The superseded unit data-flow claim incorrectly implied every completion updates length, offset, and FAT block. Errors and cancellation bypass accounting; exhaustion bypasses offset and block updates. Proposal fact 1 resolves the contradiction.

The superseded unit state explanation overgeneralized terminal cleanup to startup failures. Proposal fact 2 correctly limits clear-release-notify handling to ReadCallback and preserves the distinct cancellation sentinel and successful negative residual meanings. No deferral is needed.
